feature: Python project is a test home for spec draft and spec accept
description: spec draft and spec accept accept a root pyproject.toml, setup.py or setup.cfg as a test home, name it and pytest when they refuse, and change nothing else

specs.description: A root pyproject.toml lets spec draft proceed
specs.given: a project root with a pyproject.toml, a tests/test_x.py pytest test, no Cargo.toml, no package.json and no test.runners entry in .hexa/project.json
specs.when: the user runs `hexa spec draft` for an ADR
specs.then: the command proceeds as it does under a Cargo.toml and is not refused for lacking a test home

specs.description: A root setup.py lets spec accept proceed
specs.given: a project root with a setup.py, no Cargo.toml, no package.json and no test.runners entry
specs.when: the user runs `hexa spec accept` for a drafted spec
specs.then: the command proceeds as it does under a package.json and is not refused for lacking a test home

specs.description: A root setup.cfg alone is a test home
specs.given: a project root whose only manifest is setup.cfg, with no test.runners entry
specs.then: the command is not refused for lacking a test home

specs.description: A Python manifest below the root is not a test home
specs.given: a project whose root has no Cargo.toml, package.json, pyproject.toml, setup.py or setup.cfg and no test.runners entry, but which has sub/pyproject.toml
specs.then: the command is refused for lacking a test home

specs.description: A Python file that is not one of the three manifests does not make a test home
specs.given: a project root with only requirements.txt and tests/test_x.py, no Cargo.toml, package.json, pyproject.toml, setup.py, setup.cfg or test.runners entry
specs.then: the command is refused for lacking a test home

specs.description: Any one of the three Python manifests at the root suffices
specs.given: any project root that contains at least one of pyproject.toml, setup.py or setup.cfg, in any combination with other files, and no test.runners entry
specs.when: either `hexa spec draft` or `hexa spec accept` is run
specs.then: neither command refuses for lacking a test home

specs.description: The refusal message names a Python manifest and pytest
specs.given: a project root with no Cargo.toml, package.json, pyproject.toml, setup.py or setup.cfg and no test.runners entry
specs.then: it refuses with a message that lists a Python manifest (pyproject.toml, setup.py or setup.cfg) among the test homes alongside Cargo.toml, package.json and test.runners, and names pytest among the runners `hexa spec red` uses for a hand-written test

specs.description: The refusal no longer names only the three old test homes
specs.given: a project root with none of the test homes
specs.then: the refusal message is not one that names only Cargo.toml, package.json and test.runners; it does not omit the Python manifest or pytest

specs.description: Every refusal from either command names a Python manifest and pytest
specs.given: any project root with none of Cargo.toml, package.json, pyproject.toml, setup.py, setup.cfg and no test.runners entry, whatever other files it holds
specs.when: `hexa spec draft` or `hexa spec accept` refuses for lacking a test home
specs.then: its message lists a Python manifest among the test homes and names pytest among the runners

specs.description: Existing test homes pass as before
specs.given: three projects: one with a root Cargo.toml, one with a root package.json, and one with only a test.runners entry in .hexa/project.json
specs.when: `hexa spec draft` and `hexa spec accept` are run in each
specs.then: each command proceeds as before and is not refused for lacking a test home

specs.description: A project with no test home is still refused
specs.given: a project root with no Cargo.toml, package.json, pyproject.toml, setup.py or setup.cfg and no test.runners entry
specs.when: the user runs `hexa spec draft` or `hexa spec accept`
specs.then: the command is refused, as it was before

specs.description: spec tests still generates Rust tests only
specs.given: a Python project with a root pyproject.toml and accepted specs
specs.then: it generates no Python (.py) test files; any tests it generates are Rust tests

specs.description: Outcomes are unchanged for every project without a Python manifest
specs.given: any project root without pyproject.toml, setup.py or setup.cfg
specs.when: `hexa spec draft` or `hexa spec accept` is run
specs.then: whether it proceeds or refuses for lacking a test home is the same as before this change: it proceeds exactly when the root has a Cargo.toml or package.json or a test.runners entry is configured
